take: Record tanker rates have stranded heavy crude in the Americas, a logistics bottleneck that tightens the sour complex and widens light-heavy differentials whilst Middle East barrels stay boxed in. The same Hormuz disruption has choked Middle East LNG for seven and a half months, with four vessel attacks reported on Sunday, so freight and war-risk premia keep feeding through to both crude and gas pricing. OPEC's 2.6 million b/d demand-growth call for 2027 against just 200,000 b/d this year is a bullish positioning anchor, though the third-quarter crude and margin build already looks priced. Watch the cross-market link between record tanker earnings and product cracks: LR1 newbuildings from Emarat and CMB.TECH's fifth suezmax sale at a $59.6m gain show owners monetising these levels, whilst Ningbo-Zhoushan's simultaneous LNG, methanol and B24 bunkering signals the alternative-fuel hedge is real. Next 24 hours: Wednesday's US CPI print against oil above $90, plus any further Hormuz incident reports that could spike war-risk premia again.
